text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: model-warmup-load-failure triggered for pool=prod-gpu-az1, severity=high — 3 nodes reporting load failures

josh (oncall): getting OOMs when loading glm-2-8k into pool prod-gpu-az1. root cause looks like large checkpoint deserialization and then a CUDA OOM. throwing up sample logs below. paging infra.

megan: digging in — can you paste the full error block? also, any recent model pushes to that pool?

josh (oncall): log snip:
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:01Z] model_loader.cpp:217 load_model("glm-2-8k")
[2026-03-15T08:12:03Z] weights_deserializer.cpp:98 checksum mismatch? continuing deserialization
[2026-03-15T08:12:05Z] gpu_allocator.cpp:402 CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 12.3 GiB for KV cache
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
```
seems like deserialization might be buffering too much host memory before GPU transfer. restart of affected containers so far just shifts the failure to another node in the same pool.

carlos: no recent deploys to that model, last rollout was 3 days ago. config for that pool has compile_timeout_ms=120000 (120s).

dena: supporting customers while you triage. which customers impacted? looks like a small set of high-qps tenants pinned to prod-gpu-az1.

support-bot: Customer Impact Report (approx):
- 12 customers saw 502s for model glm-2-8k in last 10m
- error surface: "model load failed" / "service unavailable"
- top affected: acme-inc (heavy batch), shoply (sync inference)

megan: immediate mitigation options I can think of:
1) Route new load requests for glm-2-8k from prod-gpu-az1 to prod-gpu-az2 (if capacity) via routing policy change.
2) Fallback to smaller variant glm-2-8k-quant or glm-2-4k-8bit for affected customers.
3) Increase compile_timeout and enable incremental load to avoid big deserialization memory spike.

josh (oncall): trying option 2 now — triggering rollout rule to prefer glm-2-8k-quant for tenants with <=25ms SLO slack. making a canary route first.

infra-bot: Starting canary route update: route_id=canary-2161004321 target_pool=prod-gpu-az2.

sydney: FYI prod-gpu-az2 has 20% spare capacity, but not enough for a full traffic shift. recommend canary + throttled reroute + enable async loads.

megan: while canary runs, also bumping compile_timeout_ms to 300000 for the warmup path and enabling "streaming_deserialize" flag to reduce peak host memory. config change being applied to rolling agents.

josh (oncall): config patch applied to 3/6 nodes in az1, monitoring. turning on verbose loader logs for 60s.

infra-bot: Metrics update (1m): load_fail_rate prod-gpu-az1 = 62% -> after canary 36% (partial), queue depth for warmup reduced by 28%.

carlos: seeing repeated checksum warnings in logs; could be a nonfatal mismatch causing rebuffering. opening a read-only copy of weights from blobstore to validate integrity.

dena: communicating to support: telling customers we have partial mitigation (fallbacks enabled) and rolling fixes; ETA 30-45m for broader stabilization.

support-bot: Notified customers: acme-inc (PM + infra), shoply (ops). Provided workaround: pin to glm-2-8k-quant or use hosted fallback model for 1 hour.

megan: after switching to streaming_deserialize on a node, that node completed warmup successfully. log:
```
[2026-03-15T08:23:12Z] streaming_deserializer.cpp:load_chunk ok chunk=0/48
[2026-03-15T08:23:45Z] model_loader.cpp:done warmup seq_len=2048 mem_peak_host=5.1GiB mem_peak_gpu=10.9GiB
```
looks like streaming deserialization avoids the host spike. we'll keep that enabled until we root-cause the checksum warnings.

josh (oncall): handing off to megan for postmortem + cleanup. I'm going offline for the next hour. @megan take it.

megan: taking over. current state: 4/6 nodes have streaming_deserialize enabled; load_fail_rate down to 8% across pool; fallback routing active for heavy tenants. Next steps:
- finish applying streaming_deserialize to remaining nodes (in progress)
- validate blobstore checksums for the glm-2-8k artifact and reupload if corrupt
- consider permanent default to streaming_deserialize for large checkpoints
- add a defensive pre-check: estimate host memory needed before starting full deserialization and fail early to trigger fallback instead of OOM.

carlos: preliminary blobstore verify shows 1 compressed shard with checksum mismatch on upload time 2026-03-12. fetching original manifest and triggering re-upload from canonical build.

infra-bot: Reupload job queued: job_id=ru-2161004321, priority=high.

dena: once reupload completes, please post here so I can tell affected customers. support prepared a follow-up note.

megan: logging follow-up action items for postmortem:
- root cause: corrupt shard in model artifact + non-streaming deserializer causing large host memory spike -> GPU OOM during transfer
- short-term mitigations: streaming_deserialize, increased compile timeout, fallback routing to quantized variant, canary pool failover
- long-term fixes: artifact verification on upload, pre-deserialize memory estimation, make streaming_deserialize default for checkpoints > 2GB, healthcheck to pre-warm model in low-priority background before accepting traffic.

support-bot: Customer follow-up ready. Draft: "We experienced a partial service disruption for model glm-2-8k due to a corrupted artifact shard causing load failures. We have routed traffic to fallback variants and applied streaming deserialization that resolved the majority of failures. We will re-upload a verified artifact and follow up when all nodes are healthy."

megan: marking incident as "mitigated" for now. will keep thread open until artifact reupload + healthchecks pass. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident mitigated by user megan at 2026-03-15T08:42:03Z — severity downgraded to low.
